git.note: Commit is the latest merged main before this uncommitted measurement work.

runtime.serverMode: in-process route handlers with real local PostgreSQL

measurementAvailability.reason: Four read targets measured through current route handlers against the Phase 2.5 loopback PostgreSQL fixture. The earlier static findings below remain historical context; mutation scenarios remain out of scope.

dataset.scaleRationale: 20-course pages across 60 courses; two 9/18-hole tees per course; five friends plus requests and unrelated users among 30 searchable candidates; 81 ranked accounts; 60 real rounds versus the Free last-20 cap plus 10 excluded simulator rounds.

evidence.tierBehavior: The route loads real rounds before loading the owner tier and applying the Free last-20 cap.
queryCharacteristics: Dashboard Round Focus performs its own round candidate, stored insight, and viewer entitlement reads where applicable.
The main dashboard round query includes course location plus tee holes for every matching real round.
Hole-by-hole rows are loaded for the selected statistics round IDs.
One list/search query loads the requested course page.
Each returned course then triggers a separate findUnique including location, all tees, and all holes.
Static route-level shape is one list query plus N full-course queries; this is not a runtime query-count measurement.
One user search query returns candidates.
Each candidate performs a friendship query and conditionally outgoing and incoming request queries.
Static worst-case route-level shape is one plus three times N queries; this is not a runtime query-count measurement.

evidence.tierBehavior: Free global responses load up to 50 ranked rows; Premium responses honor page size up to 100.
queryCharacteristics: Blocked-user, entitlement/profile, total-count, and leaderboard-list reads precede rank calculation.
Competition rank executes an additional count query for every displayed leaderboard row.
The Free global path also reads and ranks the current user's aggregate when it exists.

localPostgresMeasurement.method: Current GET handlers, real Prisma 7.10.0 and local PostgreSQL 17.11; only requireAuth mocked; 2 warmups then 5 measured iterations per scenario, median reported. No HTTP transport.

timingDefinitions.driverRoundTripMs: Sum of node-postgres per-query round trips. Concurrent queries overlap, so this can exceed request wall time; it is not aggregate server execution time.
timingDefinitions.requestWallMs: Handler invocation through complete response body read.
timingDefinitions.serverExecutionMs: Not available in aggregate. EXPLAIN ANALYZE reports one representative execution per selected SQL shape, not total request DB time.
timingDefinitions.rowsReturnedBySql: Sum of node-postgres rowCount, not rows scanned or unique application objects.

localPostgresMeasurement.repeat: Two snapshots against the same fixture. All seven query counts, SQL row counts, result counts, payload sizes, and four classifications matched. Listed timing pairs are snapshot 1 / snapshot 2 medians.

scenarios.repeatedSql: Two location reads return 20 rows each; the base course page and batched course detail lookup each return 20 rows. Tee/hole detail reads are batched, not one SQL statement per result.
scenarios.mechanism: Duplicate base-course/location loading during full-detail response construction.

scenarios.repeatedSql: Five friendship reads for five results.
30 friendship reads and 45 friend-request reads. Five-result friend-only search uses 8 total SQL statements; 30-result mixed search uses 78.
scenarios.mechanism: Per-result friendship and conditional outgoing/incoming request queries.

scenarios.repeatedSql: 51 repeated rank-count statements for 50 listed rows plus the viewer row; 81 qualified accounts in fixture.

scenarios.mechanism: All 60 real rounds and 18 nested tee-hole objects per round are materialized before the Free last-20 cap; the SQL hole relation itself is batched.

queryPlans.method: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) in a read-only transaction on one representative parameter set per SQL shape. These are not aggregate request DB times; small-fixture sequential scans alone are not treated as defects.
